state:
Goal `core-test-1-2`, stage 2. `Core\Test::advance`, `answerHttp`, `answerSocket`, `assertCalled`
and `assertNeverCalled` have every proof: `about.md`, three examples, one attack, a bench with a
recorded figure in `docs/perf/members.ndjson`, and a Rust `covers:` test in
`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/test.rs`'s tests module. None of the attacks found a bug.

The seven members still owed are `assertEquals`, `assertEqualsDeep`, `assertCount`,
`assertContains`, `assertMatchesInline`, `assertDoesNotThrow` and `assertCompletes`. Each owes
examples, hostile, perf and tests (`bun nv proofs --owed --only ...`). They all run at the top level
of a program under `nvs run`, with no `#[Test]` class. `bun nv try <files>` runs them that way.
A bench needs `bun nv proofs --record-perf --only '<member>'`.

A Rust test of a failing assertion reads its sentence with `ctx.take_pending()`: `failed` throws
through `Fault::thrown_as(ThrownClass::TestFailure, …)`, and that route keeps the message.
`assert_called_and_assert_never_called_agree_over_one_record` is the shape. It drives members with
`nvs_runtime::call`, passes `Value::null()` for an omitted option, and drops the arguments it built.
